speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the nature of your chest pain and how long you have been experiencing the vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of forceful vomiting, alcohol use, and subsequent chest pain is highly suggestive of a Boerhaave syndrome (esophageal rupture). REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Free mediastinal air visible, suggesting perforation

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of free mediastinal air confirms esophageal rupture, consistent with Boerhaave syndrome. I will immediately consult thoracic surgery for emergency intervention. DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome
